newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Suncrush, ABI up on Coke news.
newsitem.headline: Suncrush, ABI up on Coke news.

text.p: Shares in Suncrush Ltd and Amalgamated Beverage Industries Ltd climbed on Monday on news that U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola Co invest 1.25 billion in South Africa over the next five years, dealers and analysts said.
ABI produces and distributes all the leading brands of soft drinks under franchise licence and Suncrush bottles and markets Coke brands in the country.
"The shares in both companies are up. The news is positive for both companies," a dealer said.

ABI shares climbed 60 cents, or 3.23 percent, to end at 19.20 rand on nearly 4,000 shares valued at 81,050 rand. Suncrush shares added 50 cents, or 6.02 percent, to 880 cents on a volume of 55,700 shares valued at 485,770 rand.
Dealers said the volumes were modest in line with market volumes on Monday.
Coca-Cola said it intended to double its business in South Africa as a result of the investment which would be split on a 50-50 basis between Coca-Cola and its bottlers.
Analysts said Coke's policy was to grow volumes and this augured well for the two companies. But one analyst said Pepsico Inc's entry in the country would provide competition for Suncrush.

"We will have to wait until we start seeing improvement in the market. Suncrush is still experiencing Pepsi's entry in the market (therefore) I do not see that much potential in the share," an analyst who declined to be identified said.
